PC: Prepares for laceration: Selects appropriate type and size of needle, obtains laceration tray, kidney basin, and 60 mL syringe with cap for washout
Positioning: Asks to position patient and laceration in a position such that the laceration is easy to access and is well lit
Anesthetizes: Dons gloves, infiltrates laceration completely with 1% buffered lidocaine through the wound or tests for anesthesia if LET only
Cleanses: Washes or pretends to wash laceration with 60 mL of water per 1 cm of laceration
Maintains sterility: Drapes around laceration to create a sterile field and sterility is maintained throughout procedure
Needle holder in the palm of the hand with index finger extended
Needle loaded onto needle holder between proximal and middle third of needle
Needled enters skin perpendicular to the skin
Exit at opposing end of laceration approximately equidistant from entrance bite
Leaves a short (3 cm) tail of suture for tying
When tying, hemostat placed in the center of the laceration for tying
Ties first knot with two loops
Lays suture knot lateral to the laceration
Completes suture tie by alternating hand positions, approximately 4 knots per suture
Makes corrections If suture is incorrectly placed, i.e., wound does not approximate well, suture breaks, the suture is removed and resident starts over
Discards sharps: Needle(s) safely/correctly handled and discarded
SBP: Asked for signature on the consent form
Level 1: Resident trusted to observe the laceration repair
Level 2: Resident trusted to practice the laceration repair only under proactive, full supervision as a co-activity with the supervisor
Level 3: Resident trusted to practice the laceration repair only under proactive, full supervision with the supervisor in the room and ready to step in as needed
Level 4: Resident trusted to practice the laceration repair only under reactive, on-demand supervision with supervisor immediately available and ALL findings double checked
Level 5: Resident trusted to practice the laceration repair only under reactive, on-demand supervision with supervisor immediately available and KEY findings double checked
Level 6: Resident trusted to practice the laceration repair only under reactive, on-demand supervision with supervisor distantly available (eg, by phone), findings reviewed
Level 7: Resident trusted to practice the laceration repair unsupervised

Level 8: Resident trusted to supervise others in practice of the laceration repair (where supervision means: ability to assess patient and learner needs ensuring safe, effective care and further trainee development by tailoring supervision level)
ICS: Stated that wounds are closed to minimize scaring
Stated that wound are closed to prevent wound infection
Explained the patient will be positioned in a position of comfort that best allows the procedure to be completed safely
Explained sterile/aseptic techniques will be used (to clean the skin)
Explained the patient will be given an anxiolytic – (e.g., IN Midazolam, Child Life Specialist)
Explained the patient will be given something for pain control (e.g., LET and or lidocaine)
Explained that the wound will be irrigated to minimize wound infection and remove any small foreign bodies
Explained that a needle will be used to place the sutures to bring the skin edges together
Explained that topical antibiotics and or a bulky dressing will be applied
Explained that the sutures may dissolve or be removed by the pediatrician in 5-10 days
Stated risk of possible introduction of infection
Explained alternative that the skin will eventually form a scar on its own
Stated that no intervention is an option
Explained the risk that no intervention has the disadvantages of risk of uncontrolled infection or poor cosmetics
Explained the consent form point by point
